meta.siteTitle: Rabita: Mosque and cultural centre in Oslo
meta.siteDescription: Rabita is building a new mosque and cultural centre at Calmeyers gate 8, Oslo. We are raising 100 million kroner to build it.

hero.credLine: FOUNDED 1987 · OSLO'S FIRST MOSQUE ACROSS NATIONALITIES
hero.headline: The site is ready. Now we raise the building.
hero.subhead: Oslo’s mosque across nationalities since 1987. Your gift raises seven floors at Calmeyers gate 8: prayer space by prayer space, desk by desk, shelf by shelf.

history.name: History
history.title: Founded in {year}.
history.body: The first mosque in Oslo not tied to one nationality: a place for Muslims in Norway, wherever they came from. The building we are raising makes room for all of it.

family.name: Community
family.title: {members} members. One community.
family.body: From more than {nationalities} nationalities. We stand together, in prayer and in learning, in joy and in grief, with each other and with our neighbours.

learning.name: Learning
learning.title: Over {pupils} pupils.
learning.body: Evening talks, Quran classes for children, Arabic for beginners, calligraphy and philosophy. Waiting lists in every class.

volunteer.name: Volunteering
volunteer.title: {volunteers} volunteers, all year.
volunteer.body: Around {visitors} visitors a week. Volunteers in yellow vests hand out food, coordinate with the district and stand with neighbours in good times and bad.

statement.before: Oslo's first mosque belonging to no single nationality.
statement.accent: Now we are making room for everyone it brought together.

buildingRises.heading: From foundation to prayer hall.
buildingRises.lede: Scroll to see the building take shape, seven floors above and below the street, each with its purpose. Every kroner builds a layer.

intro.body: The old mosque was demolished during Ramadan 2025. Seven floors are to go up. Scroll to watch them arrive.

prayer.name: PRAYER HALL

school.body: Nineteen teachers, four hundred pupils, waiting lists in every class. Real daylight classrooms.

library.body: Reading hall, seminar rooms, a youth section. Somewhere to study that isn't home.

youth.name: YOUTH CLUB
youth.headline: Somewhere to be on a Friday night.
youth.body: Youth club, offices for volunteers, and a studio for podcasts and recordings.

entrance.body: Café, reception and the main entrance for the congregation and the city. No threshold.

building.title: Seven floors on one address.
building.lede: A mosque, a school, a library, a kitchen and a hall on one plot at Calmeyers gate 8 — two floors below the street, five above. The old mosque was demolished in 2025. What rises in its place is one building doing the work of five, with its ground floor open to the street.
building.brief: The old mosque was demolished in 2025. What replaces it is one building doing the work of five, on a 6 762 square metre plot, designed so the ground floor stays open to the street rather than turning its back on it.

items.title: Prayer halls
items.body: Room for 500 women and 2 000 men across three floors, against 100 places for women today.

items.title: The school
items.body: The largest Arabic school in Norway, 400 pupils and 19 teachers, in daylight classrooms.

items.title: Library and youth
items.body: A reading hall and seminar rooms open to the district, with a youth club and a studio.

items.title: Entrance and cafe
items.body: A ground floor open to the whole city, with no threshold between the street and the building.

building.ledeShort: A mosque, school, library, kitchen and hall on one plot at Calmeyers gate 8. Ground floor open to the street.

money.title: Costed room by room.
money.lede: Every krone is tied to something physical in the building, and the accounts that prove it are public.
money.brief: The campaign is 100 million kroner across three phases. 26 995 179 kroner is in, which is 26 per cent, and the phase it belongs to is stated rather than implied. Rental apartments are part of the building specifically so maintenance never consumes the organisation again.

items.title: Annual accounts

donors.brief: The foundation wall is not a plaque in a corridor. It is part of the structure, and it records who paid for the building the congregation will use for the next hundred years.

give.brief: A monthly gift is what lets the building be planned rather than hoped for. Five hundred kroner a month for three years funds one prayer place, and the ladder above that is costed room by room.

privacyPage.title: Short and simple.
privacyPage.lede: We collect as little as possible, store it securely, and build the site so it works for everyone.

privacy.heading: Privacy
privacy.controller: The data controller is Rabita, org.nr. {orgNr}, at Calmeyers gate 8, Oslo.
privacy.dataWeCollect: We store name, email, phone number and donation details to process gifts and tax deductions. Site analytics are anonymous.
privacy.fnr: National identity number is collected only where you opt in for tax deduction. It is encrypted at rest, access-restricted, and deleted after the statutory period.
privacy.hosting: The site is hosted in the EEA. We do not use third-party tracking before you consent.
privacy.rights: You have the right to access, rectify and delete. Write to us and we reply within 30 days.

a11y.heading: Universal design
a11y.wcag: We build to WCAG 2.1 AA. Where anything falls short, write to us. We fix on a rolling basis.

list.contrast: Colour contrast is tested, with particular attention to the gold accent.
list.keyboard: All functionality is keyboard-operable, including the giving sheet (Escape closes).
list.textsize: Text size controls at the top of every page, remembered on your device.
list.rtl: The site is built with logical properties, so right-to-left for Arabic works naturally.
list.altText: Images and illustrations have alt text; pure decoration is hidden from screen readers.

a11y.feedback: Feedback? Write to us. We prioritise all accessibility reports.

servicesIndex.title: Nikah, janaza, shahada and more.
servicesIndex.lede: Religious services, guidance, teaching and work out in the community. Every enquiry is handled discreetly.

nikah.title: Nikah: wedding ceremony
nikah.body: The religious ceremony, once the marriage is registered.
nikah.longBody: Nikah is the Islamic marriage contract, entered into in accordance with Islamic principles. Rabita holds the religious nikah in the mosque, led by an imam. The couple must already be legally married and present a valid marriage certificate.
nikah.offerLede: Nikah at Rabita is led by an imam and held in the mosque. Get in touch in good time and we will find a date together.

offer.title: Before the nikah
offer.body: The couple must already be legally married and present a valid marriage certificate.
offer.detail: Rabita does not perform a religious nikah unless the civil marriage has been registered first.

offer.title: How the ceremony works
offer.body: The couple attend with the necessary witnesses and the imam leads the ceremony. Both parties confirm that they are entering the marriage of their own free will.
offer.detail: The marriage contract is concluded in the presence of witnesses, and the mahr is agreed between the parties as part of the Islamic marriage.

offer.title: The imam's guidance
offer.body: The imam offers advice and reminders about marriage and what the spouses owe one another.
offer.detail: About the importance of building a home marked by respect, care and mercy.

offer.title: A ceremony, not a wedding party
offer.body: Family and a few close relatives may attend.
offer.detail: Nikah at Rabita is a religious ceremony. The mosque does not accommodate large gatherings, catering or extensive celebration. Bookings and questions: post@rabita.no

janaza.title: Janaza: funeral
janaza.body: The Janazah prayer in the mosque, and guidance for the family.
janaza.longBody: In Islamic faith the end of a life has its own dignified frame. When someone passes away, family and community gather for the Janazah prayer — the last prayer for the deceased and a final farewell before burial. Rabita holds the Janazah prayer in the mosque, led by an imam.
janaza.offerLede: In a time of grief we want to make the religious farewell as simple and as dignified as possible for the family.

offer.title: The Janazah prayer
offer.body: The prayer is held in the mosque and led by an imam, with family, friends and others from the community present.
offer.detail: Janazah is the Muslim community’s last prayer for the deceased, and a final farewell before the burial.

offer.title: The ritual washing
offer.body: Rabita can help the family with guidance and put them in contact with people who can carry out the washing of the deceased.
offer.detail: The washing is performed in accordance with Islamic tradition.

offer.title: What the funeral director does
offer.body: Handling of the deceased, transport, the coffin and coordination with the cemetery are not done by Rabita.
offer.detail: These are handled by the funeral directors, whom we work with when needed. The family contacts the funeral director for the practical side of the burial.

offer.title: Get in touch
offer.body: Rabita assists with the religious part and the Janazah prayer.
offer.detail: For questions or to arrange a time: post@rabita.no

shahada.title: Shahada: declaration of faith
shahada.body: An open conversation about Islam, and guidance if you want to take shahada.
shahada.longBody: Are you curious about Islam, do you want to learn more about the faith, or do you have questions you would like to talk through with someone? At Rabita you are welcome to an open conversation with no obligation. Wherever you are in that process, we meet you with respect and on your own terms.
shahada.offerLede: You do not need to have decided anything to get in touch. Some want to know more, some want guidance, and some have reached the point of wanting to take the shahada.

offer.title: A conversation with no obligation
offer.body: You are welcome to an open conversation, wherever you are in the process.
offer.detail: We meet you with respect and on your own terms. You do not need to have made up your mind about anything.

offer.title: Questions and guidance
offer.body: Our imams answer questions, explain the basics of Islam and offer religious guidance.
offer.detail: Some get in touch because they want to know more about Islam. Others have been exploring the faith for a while and want guidance.

offer.title: Shahada
offer.body: For those who have decided to become Muslim, Rabita offers guidance around the shahada — the Islamic declaration of faith.

offer.title: The time afterwards
offer.body: There can be a great many new questions when you are new to the faith.
offer.detail: We want Rabita to be a place where you also find knowledge, community and support going forward.

counselling.title: Counselling and mediation
counselling.body: Confidential conversations and mediation with an imam or a female counsellor.
counselling.longBody: Life can bring periods where conflict, difficulties in a relationship or other crises become hard to handle alone. Rabita offers confidential conversations and mediation with an imam or a female counsellor. The conversations rest on trust and are treated in confidence.
counselling.offerTitle: Someone who listens, and who knows the ground
counselling.offerLede: We meet people in all kinds of situations — difficulties between spouses, conflict within a family, conflict between generations, or anything else that has become hard to carry.

offer.title: Confidential conversations
offer.body: A conversation with an imam or a female counsellor, for anyone who needs someone to listen and to offer advice and guidance.
offer.detail: What is said is treated in confidence, with respect and discretion, within the obligations that follow from Norwegian law.

offer.title: Mediation
offer.body: In mediation we try to create a safe and neutral room where both parties can talk, be heard and work towards a solution.
offer.detail: The aim is not to take sides, but to help dialogue, understanding and, where it is possible, reconciliation.

offer.title: We know the communities
offer.body: Some people find they need guidance that also takes their faith, culture or family situation into account.
offer.detail: This is where the mosque can have a particular role. We know the communities, the languages, and the religious and cultural frames many of the people who come to us live within.

offer.title: When a case needs more
offer.body: This does not replace professional health care, family counselling, legal aid or other public services.
offer.detail: When a case calls for other or more specialised help, we will encourage contact with the right agency. Get in touch: post@rabita.no

hajj-umrah.title: Hajj and umrah
hajj-umrah.body: Organised pilgrimages to Mecca, from Rabita’s own office.
hajj-umrah.longBody: Hajj, the pilgrimage to Mecca, is the fifth pillar of Islam and an obligation on every Muslim with the physical and financial means to make the journey. Umrah is the lesser pilgrimage and can be performed through most of the year. The hajj and umrah office sits in Rabita’s own premises and is run by a committed team of volunteers with years of experience.
hajj-umrah.offerTitle: The journey to Mecca, well organised
hajj-umrah.offerLede: For many people hajj and umrah are among the largest journeys they will make. Our aim is to make the trip as safe and as clear as possible, so the time goes to what the journey is actually for.

offer.title: Organised package trips
offer.body: The hajj and umrah office is based in Rabita’s premises and run by volunteers with long experience.
offer.detail: Over the years it has grown into one of the largest operators in Norway for organised pilgrimages to Mecca.

offer.title: We handle the practical side
offer.body: The visa process, travel documentation, flights, accommodation and any other coordination needed.
offer.detail: We put weight on offering good, complete travel packages at favourable prices.

offer.title: Preparation before you leave
offer.body: Travellers are given information and guidance on how hajj and umrah are performed.
offer.detail: That gives both first-time and more experienced travellers the chance to prepare for the religious as well as the practical sides of the journey.

offer.title: When the trips run
offer.body: Hajj runs every year in the month of Dhul Hijjah. Umrah normally two to three times a year.
offer.detail: Umrah trips are mostly placed in the school holidays, which makes it easier for families with children to take part. Telephone 40 29 20 20 · hajjogumrah@gmail.com

skole.title: Rabita school
skole.body: Weekend school in Arabic, the Quran and Islamic studies, for children aged 6 to 16.
skole.longBody: Rabita’s Arabic school is a weekend school for children and young people aged 6 to 16, and one of our largest and longest-established offerings for children and families. In 2025 it had 225 pupils across 13 classes.
skole.offerLede: We want the children to have a place where language, faith, identity and community belong together naturally.

offer.title: Weekend school for ages 6 to 16
offer.body: One of our largest and longest-established offerings for children and families.
offer.detail: In 2025 the school had 225 pupils across 13 classes.

offer.title: Arabic, the Quran and Islamic studies
offer.body: The teaching follows a clear pedagogical structure.
offer.detail: The aim is that the children develop good language skills, come to know their religious and cultural heritage, build friendships and grow up with a secure identity as Norwegian Muslims.

offer.title: The teachers
offer.body: Every permanent teacher holds a teaching qualification and works day to day within Norwegian educational institutions.

offer.title: Enrolment and contact
offer.body: Information about registration and available places is announced through Rabita’s own channels.
offer.detail: Questions about the teaching, year groups, registration or available places: undervisning@arabiskald.no

koran.title: Quran and Arabic
koran.body: Quran and Arabic teaching for children, young people and adults.
koran.longBody: Knowledge holds a central place in Islam. Through our teaching Rabita wants to make it possible for children and adults alike to come closer to the Quran, to learn Arabic, and to build knowledge in a safe and welcoming place to learn.
koran.offerTitle: Closer to the Quran, and to the language it came in
koran.offerLede: Teaching is adapted to each participant’s age and prior knowledge, so that it is possible to start whatever level you are at.

offer.title: Quran teaching
offer.body: Learning the Quran is about more than being able to read a text.
offer.detail: It is about understanding your faith, developing your relationship with God, and carrying the Quran’s values and guidance into everyday life. Contact: kunnskap@rabita.no

offer.title: Every level
offer.body: Some meet the Arabic alphabet for the first time; others want to develop their reading, pronunciation and recitation.
offer.detail: Rabita offers Quran teaching for both children and adults at a range of levels.

offer.title: Arabic for adults
offer.body: For beginners, and for anyone who wants to become more confident reading, writing and understanding Arabic.
offer.detail: Contact: undervisning@rabita.no

offer.title: The language and the source
offer.body: For some the goal is to communicate better in Arabic. For others it is fuller access to the Quran and to Islamic sources in the original.
offer.detail: The Quran was revealed in Arabic, and central parts of Islamic practice are bound to the language.

kurs.title: Calligraphy and geometry
kurs.body: Courses in Islamic calligraphy and geometric art.
kurs.longBody: Art and beauty have held an important place in the Islamic tradition for centuries. At Rabita we want to keep that tradition alive and within reach of new generations, through courses where traditional craft, history, precision and creative work meet.
kurs.offerLede: Calligraphy is closely bound to the Quran and to the wish to give the written word a beautiful and dignified form. With geometry, it is among the most characteristic expressions of Islamic art.

offer.title: Calligraphy with Ustadh Khalid Casado
offer.body: Participants work on classical letter proportions, technique and composition under individual guidance.
offer.detail: He holds diplomas from the master calligraphers Hasan Celebi, Ferhat Kurlu and Nuria Garcia Masip in the Ottoman tradition.

offer.title: Geometry with Samira Mian
offer.body: With compass and ruler, participants learn to construct the precise and complex patterns that have marked Islamic art and architecture for centuries.
offer.detail: The teaching also opens up the form’s history, from Spain in the west to India in the east, and participants work with colour and watercolour to make something of their own.

offer.title: Participants from several countries
offer.body: Our courses have drawn participants from Germany, Spain and England among others.

offer.title: Dates and enrolment
offer.body: Courses run through the year and are announced on rabita.no and on our social media.
offer.detail: For questions or more information: post@rabita.no

veivisere.title: Muslim guides
veivisere.body: School visits where young Muslims meet pupils face to face.
veivisere.longBody: Muslimske veivisere is a dialogue and knowledge programme set up to counter prejudice and discrimination against Norwegian Muslims. Through school visits, young Muslim guides meet pupils face to face and speak openly about faith, identity, belonging, and what it is like to grow up and live as a Muslim in Norway.
veivisere.offerTitle: What happens to prejudice when people actually meet?
veivisere.offerLede: The aim is simple, and it matters: more knowledge, less distance, fewer prejudices.

offer.title: School visits
offer.body: Young guides speak openly about faith, identity and belonging, and about growing up Muslim in Norway.
offer.detail: Pupils get to ask questions — including the difficult ones there is not always a natural place to ask.

offer.title: More than 200 schools
offer.body: Since 2025 the guides have visited over 200 schools and met more than 10,000 pupils.
offer.detail: Schools can also visit the mosque, take a tour and meet the guides on their own ground.

offer.title: Where it came from
offer.body: Developed by Det Islamske Forbundet – Rabita and Minotenk, modelled on the Sami and Jewish guide schemes.
offer.detail: It was later written into the government’s Action Plan against Muslim Hostility 2025–2030, presented in December 2024.

offer.title: Who runs it
offer.body: The scheme is owned today by Muslimsk Dialognettverk and operated by Det Islamske Forbundet – Rabita.
offer.detail: The work is done with Minotenk and the Faculty of Theology at the University of Oslo.

norsk.title: Norwegian and taking part
norsk.body: Norwegian classes for adults who fall outside the ordinary provision.
norsk.longBody: Knowing the language of the country you live in is about far more than making yourself understood. It is about talking to your children’s school, understanding a letter from the authorities, applying for work, taking an education, following the public debate, and taking part in society on your own terms.
norsk.offerTitle: Language is what lets people take part
norsk.offerLede: We offer Norwegian teaching for adults who need somewhere accessible to learn and to practise.

offer.title: For those who fall outside
offer.body: Some have no right to free Norwegian tuition. Others have lived in Norway for years but never had the chance to learn the language well enough.
offer.detail: The classes are aimed particularly at people whose Norwegian tuition is not covered by the public system.

offer.title: More than grammar
offer.body: The aim is that participants become more confident and more independent in meeting working life, public services, school and education.
offer.detail: And that they get a real chance to take an active part in society.

offer.title: A natural part of being a mosque
offer.body: We meet people at every stage of life, including people the public services do not always reach.
offer.detail: We want to use that trust and closeness to open more doors into Norwegian society.

offer.title: Enrolment
offer.body: For information about the Norwegian classes, courses and how to sign up.
offer.detail: Get in touch with Rabita at post@rabita.no

ungdom.title: Norges Unge Muslimer
ungdom.body: Rabita’s youth organisation, run by and for young people.
ungdom.longBody: Young people need more than somewhere to be. They need community, good role models, knowledge, and places where they can develop, take responsibility and feel they belong. Norges Unge Muslimer is Rabita’s youth organisation, with a board of its own.
ungdom.offerTitle: Room to make, to lead and to shape
ungdom.offerLede: We do not just want to put on activities for young people. We want to give them real room to make things, to lead and to shape what happens.

offer.title: Run by young people
offer.body: The organisation is run by and for young people, with an independent board.
offer.detail: Planning and running activities gives them real experience of working together, of organising, of responsibility and of leadership.

offer.title: Camps, courses and trips
offer.body: Through the year NUM runs camps, courses and theme evenings, conferences, social activities, trips and larger events.
offer.detail: The networks that form around the activities matter as much as the activities themselves.

offer.title: Jenter i fokus and Gutter i fokus
offer.body: Two focused programmes for ages 11 to 15, combining Islamic teaching with guidance, activities and a social community.
offer.detail: At an age where many begin to explore questions of faith, identity, friendship and expectation, we want to offer steady places to meet, with trusted adults and good role models.

offer.title: Prevention, and who we work with
offer.body: Preventing exclusion and crime, psychosocial safety, identity and participation are central parts of the work.
offer.detail: We work with the Norwegian Correctional Service, SALTO and Bydel Gamle Oslo among others.

barn-og-familie.title: Children and family
barn-og-familie.body: Activities and places to meet for children and families, all year round.
barn-og-familie.longBody: Rabita should be a place where children too collect good memories, build friendships and feel the pleasure of being part of something larger. So through the year we run a range of activities and gatherings for children and families.
barn-og-familie.offerTitle: Somewhere the children can call theirs too
barn-og-familie.offerLede: For us this work is about belonging — for the children, and for the families around them.

offer.title: The festivals
offer.body: Through Id for alle, the Ramadan workshop and other markings, we want to build a good frame around our festivals.
offer.detail: Faith and tradition are not passed on through teaching alone, but through experiences, company and good memories.

offer.title: Camps and trips
offer.body: Through the year we run camps, outings, trips and a range of social activities for children and families.

offer.title: Simply meeting
offer.body: Some activities belong to a particular occasion; others are simply about meeting and getting to know one another across families and generations.

offer.title: When things happen
offer.body: Information about upcoming family activities, events and sign-up is published as it is set.
offer.detail: On Rabita’s website and on our social media.

fosterhjem.title: Become a foster family
fosterhjem.body: Information and guidance for families considering fostering.
fosterhjem.longBody: There are children and young people in Oslo who for various reasons cannot live with their parents, and who need a safe and stable home. Among them are children with a Muslim background waiting for a family who can give them care, safety and belonging.
fosterhjem.offerTitle: Perhaps it starts with a conversation
fosterhjem.offerLede: You do not have to have decided anything before you get in touch. At Rabita you can take the first step with no obligation at all.

offer.title: Why it matters
offer.body: When a child has to move away from their own family, that is already a large upheaval in their life.
offer.detail: For some children it can mean a great deal to come to a family who also understands their religious and cultural background — while the most important thing is always that the child gets a safe and good home.

offer.title: Bro til omsorg
offer.body: Through the project Bro til omsorg, Rabita works with Oslo’s child and family agency to inform and recruit Muslim foster families.
offer.detail: The project is funded by Bufdir.

offer.title: The questions you are sitting with
offer.body: Who can become a foster parent? What is required? How does the process work? And what would it mean for the family and for everyday life?
offer.detail: Our role is to answer questions, give information, and be a bridge between families considering opening their home to a child and Oslo’s child and family agency.

offer.title: Take the first step
offer.body: You can contact us with no obligation for information and guidance on what fostering involves.

aboutPage.title: Rabita since 1987.
aboutPage.lede: From a flat in Grønland to one of the largest and oldest mosques in Norway.
aboutPage.historyHeading: A congregation that outgrew its building.
aboutPage.quote: A place where faith and citizenship go together.

factNotes.founded: The start of our journey in Oslo

history.p1: Rabita was founded in 1987 as the first mosque in Oslo not tied to a single nationality. The idea was simple: a place for Muslims in Norway, regardless of where they came from.
history.p2: The congregation grew, the school was established, and the cultural centre became part of civil society in Oslo. The old building ran out of space long ago.
history.p3: In October {year} King Harald V and Crown Prince Haakon visited the mosque, the first royal visit to a mosque in Norway. We continue to work with the same aim: a place where faith and civic life belong together.

about.heading: Living in the heart of Oslo.
about.body1: A rare chance to live in the heart of Oslo, centrally placed and a short walk from government institutions, tourist attractions, major transport hubs and large shopping centres — and, not least, in the same building as the Oslo Mosque.
about.body2: The project comprises modern apartments and a broad range of facilities, among them a café, restaurants, a multi-purpose hall, a roof terrace and sheltered outdoor areas.

modern.title: Modern apartments
modern.body: Efficient layouts, good materials and a light design.

central.title: Central location
central.body: Walking distance to Oslo City, the Storting and the main transport hubs.

about.mapCaption: Walking times are measured along real pedestrian routes, not in a straight line.

location.heading: Close to everything that matters.
location.lede: Calmeyers gate sits in an attractive, well-established part of Oslo, within walking distance of the city's most important functions.
items: 5–10 minutes on foot to Oslo City, the Storting and the central parts of town
A short walk to Grünerløkka, with its wide choice of cafés, restaurants and shops
Close to the main transport hubs — Jernbanetorget, Stortinget and Tøyen
location.close: It is a rare combination: central access, and a quiet place to live.

imams.heading: The people who lead the prayer.
imams.lede: One theological leader and two imams. You meet them at Friday prayer, in the classes, and in the conversation afterwards.

amara.bio: Trained at the Sharia Faculty of the University of Beirut and in pedagogy at Oslo University College. A teacher in Bærum from 2001 to 2008, and a frequent lecturer in mosques across Norway and Europe.

andreas.bio: Teaches the Islamic-studies course in Norwegian and gives regular lectures for members and visitors. The voice of the adhan at the street iftar.

aldiri.bio: Joined as imam in 2025. Holds a doctorate, with deep expertise in Islamic scholarship, dialogue, youth work and communication.

fremdrift.title: From vision to finished building.
fremdrift.lede: The most pivotal years of the project now lie ahead. The old mosque has been demolished and the ground cleared. We now begin the work of building a mosque that will serve generations to come.
fremdrift.aheadHeading: The years in front of us.
fremdrift.aheadLede: As we approach the end of 2025, we stand at a defining moment in the project. The old mosque is now part of our history. The building has been dismantled and the site has been cleared. For many years it was our shared home. Now we open the door to something greater, more beautiful and more sustainable. The first two phases have been completed. We now enter the next, and most crucial, phase: the construction of the mosque itself.

vision.name: Vision
vision.body: After many years in our former mosque, the need for a larger space became increasingly clear. The old building was worn down, expensive to maintain, and no longer met the needs of our growing community. That is why a bold new vision was launched: to tear down the existing structure and build a new, modern Islamic centre — with a mosque spanning multiple floors, a school, a library, a youth club, a multi-purpose hall and residential units.

preparation.name: Preparation
preparation.body: The first official steps toward a new mosque were taken in 2019, when we entered a long-term collaboration with architect Håvard Lindgard Fagernes, who developed the initial design sketches. In 2022 the project received full approval from the municipality, and by 2024 it was opened to bids from some of the country's leading construction firms. These milestones laid a solid foundation and marked the beginning of a new chapter: the mosque of the future.

demolition.name: Demolition
demolition.body: After several years of ideas, sketches and careful planning, the first major milestone was reached in 2025. During Ramadan that year, demolition began on the 19th-century building that had served as our mosque for generations. We carried with us the memories and stories shaped within its walls, while knowing in our hearts that this was the beginning of something new.

construction.name: Construction
construction.body: In the first quarter of 2026, the goal is to begin construction of the foundation, main structure and external facade. This is the most critical phase of the project, a defining milestone that brings us closer to the vision of a new, modern mosque in the heart of Oslo.

interior.name: Interior
interior.body: By the end of 2027, our goal is to complete the interior work in the basement, first floor and second floor. These levels will form the heart of the building, with prayer areas spread across three floors, including wudu facilities and changing rooms.

completion.name: Completion
completion.body: In the final phase, the aim is to complete the upper floors. The third floor will be dedicated to education, with modern classrooms and flexible spaces for weekend school, courses and lectures. The fourth floor will house offices, meeting rooms, a studio and a large youth club. The fifth and sixth floors will contain residential apartments, providing stable income to help sustain the mosque's upkeep and community activities for years to come.

fremdrift.goalNote: The build cost is given in euro, as it is budgeted per phase. Our fundraising is in kroner and covers a share of it — the two are not the same figure, and we do not convert one into the other.
